editorial.tldr: On Oct 21, a paper on extracting materials data from literature with ML and LLMs appeared alongside NVIDIA's Kumo Relational, which claims to beat supervised ML on relational data with no training. The thread is loosely linked by the 'machine learning' label rather than a single event.
editorial.whats_new: A tutorial on physics-constrained ML (Oct 23) presents a modular framework for hybrid modeling, optimization and control that builds domain constraints into models.
editorial.why_it_matters: Two items push ML toward less task-specific training (LLM extraction, training-free relational prediction); the third pushes toward encoding first-principles constraints. Both change what you build versus buy.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before adopting Kumo Relational, rerun it against your own supervised baseline on your relational data; treat the claim as unverified until you do.
